claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start with the first check. To determine your eligibility, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please tell me:
- The name(s) of the child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So we're assessing eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 8 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, let me navigate to the next check in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to ask about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

For context: At age 8, most children aren't in paid work, so I'm expecting the answer is yes, but I need to confirm this with you.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh no, he's only 8! He doesn't work at all - he's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Of course! That makes perfect sense at age 8. Alex is not in paid work and is in primary school. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about Alex's benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(Again, at age 8, this is unlikely, but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about Alex's apprenticeship status:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

At age 8 in primary school, the answer is almost certainly no, but I need to confirm for the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not! He's only 8 and in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Exactly! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

**Can you tell me about your residency situation?** Do any of these apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common situation
2. **You have settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. **You have pre-settled status** under the EU Settlement Scheme and are:
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - Actively seeking work (jobseeker), OR
   - Have sufficient resources to support yourself and family, OR
   - A student with sufficient resources, OR
   - A family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant** living abroad in certain qualifying countries

Which of these best describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't live in the UK, actually. I'm abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying! So you're currently living abroad. To help me determine if you still qualify for Child Benefit, I need to understand more about your situation.

**Can you tell me:**

1. **What's your employment or status situation?** Are you:
   - Working abroad?
   - A Crown servant (civil servant, diplomat, military, etc.) posted abroad?
   - Studying?
   - Something else?

2. **Do you have any specific immigration status** such as:
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
   - Other visa/status?

3. **Which country are you currently in?**

These details will help me determine if you meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility, as there are special circumstances that can allow people living abroad to still receive it.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm just living abroad - I don't work for the government or anything like that. I don't have settled or pre-settled status. I'm not a Crown servant.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on what you've told me, it sounds like you're living abroad but don't fall into any of the special categories that would allow you to claim Child Benefit (such as being a Crown servant, having EU Settlement Scheme status, or meeting other specific criteria).

Let me confirm this to make sure I have the full picture:

**So to clarify:**
- You normally live abroad (not the UK)
- You're not working as a Crown servant or in a qualifying government role
- You don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You're not in any of the other special circumstances categories

Is that correct? And just to confirm - **do you have any connection to the UK** (such as still being considered normally resident there for any reason, or planning to return)?

Based on what you've described, it appears you may not meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit, but I want to make sure I have all the details before I give you my final assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's correct - I don't have any of those special circumstances. I just live abroad now with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Based on the information you've provided, I can now give you my assessment regarding Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Result: **NOT ELIGIBLE** ❌

I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex at this time.

### Why:

While Alex meets all the child-specific eligibility requirements (he's 8 years old, not working full-time, doesn't receive benefits in his own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship), **you do not meet the residency requirements** for Child Benefit.

Child Benefit requires the claimant to normally live in the UK, or to fall into specific exceptions such as:
- Being a Crown servant posted abroad
- Having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with qualifying circumstances)
- Other special circumstances

Since you're living abroad without any of these qualifying circumstances, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex.

### What you can do:

1. **If your circumstances change** - For example, if you return to live in the UK, or if you gain a qualifying status, you would need to reapply.

2. **Contact HMRC** - For the most up-to-date advice specific to your situation, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit team:
   - Phone: 0300 200 3100
   - Website: www.gov.uk/child-benefit

3. **Check other benefits** - You may be eligible for other support depending on your country and circumstances. Check with local authorities where you're living.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16) and meets the initial eligibility criteria: he is not working full-time, does not receive benefits in his own right, and is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. However, the claimant does not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit. The claimant lives abroad and does not fall into any of the special circumstances that would allow them to claim while living outside the UK (such as being a Crown servant, having EU Settlement Scheme status, or other qualifying circumstances). Therefore, Alex is ineligible for Child Benefit due to the claimant's failure to meet residency requirements.
arguments.overall_reasoning: While Alex would otherwise qualify as a child under 16 with no disqualifying factors, the claimant does not meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit. Living abroad without qualifying circumstances (Crown servant status, EU Settlement Scheme status, or other special provisions) means the claimant cannot receive Child Benefit for Alex. The residency requirement is a fundamental eligibility criterion that must be met regardless of the child's eligibility status."
